best_for: People who watch a lot of YouTube on a computer and want no ads and no Google account, and who can live with beta software that sometimes breaks.
description:
FreeTube is a desktop app for watching YouTube, made by the FreeTube Team as open source software under the AGPL 3. Its layout looks a lot like YouTube's, so you do not have to learn a new way to browse, and volunteers translate it into many languages through Weblate.

You can browse Trending, jump through a video with its chapters, and take a screenshot of any frame. Pop a video into a mini player while you keep browsing, or open several windows at once. Browser extensions such as LibRedirect send YouTube links straight into FreeTube, and you can hand any video to an outside player if you prefer one. Themes change the look, and an option shows only family-friendly content.

points.title: Subscriptions without a Google account
points.text: You follow channels without signing in. Subscriptions, playlists and history stay on your device, and you can import your subscriptions from YouTube.

points.title: No ads, sponsor segments skipped
points.text: Videos play without ads, and SponsorBlock and DeArrow are built in. Profiles let you split subscriptions into smaller feeds.

points.title: Still a beta
points.text: The project calls FreeTube beta software, so expect bugs and gaps. It does not use the official YouTube API and reads YouTube itself, or an Invidious instance if you choose.

points.title: Private, not invisible
points.text: YouTube can still see the video requests and your IP address. The project suggests a VPN or Tor if that matters to you, and supports proxies.

points.title: Current systems only
points.text: Official support is Windows 10 or later and macOS 13 or later. Windows builds come for x64 and Arm64, and macOS has Intel and Apple silicon images.

points.title: Homebrew is off the table
points.text: The Homebrew cask was disabled on 2026-09-01 because it failed Apple's Gatekeeper check. Mac users should take the disk image from the project's releases instead.

points.title: Where older versions live
points.text: The Flatpak is verified on Flathub, for x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 33 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
